message.content:
Ты разведчик в репозитории LiveSpec. Рабочее дерево: /private/tmp/ls-director/wt (git worktree; только ЧТЕНИЕ, ничего не менять и не коммитить).

Задача: инвентарь всех проверок, которые могут заблокировать работу или push. Каталоги: `guardrails/` (~90 файлов), `hooks/`, `.github/workflows/`, плюс git-хуки, если они прописаны в репозитории.

Для КАЖДОЙ проверки (скрипт/gate/hook) запиши:
1. Путь к файлу.
2. Когда срабатывает: pre-commit / pre-push / CI / на каждый ход агента / вызывается вручную. Это надо доказать: найди, кто её вызывает (grep по имени файла в `.github/workflows/`, `guardrails/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/`, `install.sh`, `settings.json`). Если никто не вызывает — так и напиши: «сирота».
3. Что она проверяет — одно предложение.
4. **Главное:** одним предложением ответь, какую РЕАЛЬНУЮ потерю она предотвращает. Затем поставь метку:
   - `ЗАЩИЩАЕТ` — бережёт пользовательские данные/файлы, секреты, обратимость, компиляцию/типы/схему, продуктовые тесты, соответствие сгенерированного артефакта его источнику.
   - `САМОРЕФЕРЕНТНО` — охраняет только внутренний формат самого LiveSpec: число правил/файлов, собственный манифест гейтов, доказательство того, что гейт умеет падать, стилистические лимиты находок, ритуальные ежедневные записи, совпадение дублирующих списков, придуманные числовые бюджеты текста.
   - `ДУБЛЬ` — то же самое уже делает другой тест или CI.
   - `НЕЯСНО` — не смог определить, объясни почему.

Также найди и перечисли отдельно:
- все места, где заданы числовые пороги/бюджеты/лимиты (ceilings, budgets, max counts, ratchets) — путь, строка, само число, что оно ограничивает;
- «гейты, проверяющие гейты» — проверки, единственный предмет которых другая проверка или её манифест;
- gate a (prover record) и gate s (skill review): где их код, кто их зовёт, какие у них есть поблажки (carve-outs) — назови каждую.

Работай через bash (ls, grep -rn, sed, head). Файлы в guardrails/ читай выборочно — обычно хватает первых 40 строк и docstring/комментария вверху.

Верни ОДИН markdown-документ на русском: сводная таблица (файл · когда · что проверяет · какую потерю предотвращает · метка), затем три списка (пороги, гейты-над-гейтами, gate a / gate s). В конце — счётчик: сколько ЗАЩИЩАЕТ, сколько САМОРЕФЕРЕНТНО, сколько ДУБЛЬ, сколько НЕЯСНО, сколько сирот. Твой финальный текст — это и есть результат.

- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

=== install.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install.sh — copies live-spec skills into ~/.claude/skills/
# Idempotent: backs up any existing skill with a timestamp before overwriting.
# Usage: ./install.sh

set -euo pipefail

SKILLS_SRC="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/skills" && pwd)"
SKILLS_DEST="$HOME/.claude/skills"
TIMESTAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"

mkdir -p "$SKILLS_DEST"  # a fresh machine has no skills home yet (E-21's fresh-install promise)

echo "live-spec install — copying skills to $SKILLS_DEST"
echo "Timestamp for backups: $TIMESTAMP"
echo ""

for skill_dir in "$SKILLS_SRC"/*/; do
  skill_name="$(basename "$skill_dir")"
  if [ -e "$skill_dir/.git" ]; then
    echo "  $skill_name — SKIPPED (external skill's canonical clone; scripts/install-external-skills.sh owns it)"
    continue
  fi
  dest="$SKILLS_DEST/$skill_name"

  if [ -d "$dest" ]; then
    backup_home="$SKILLS_DEST-attic"
    mkdir -p "$backup_home"
    backup="$backup_home/$skill_name.bak_$TIMESTAMP"
    echo "  $skill_name — backing up existing to $backup"
    cp -r "$dest" "$backup"
  else
    echo "  $skill_name — new install"
  fi

  cp -r "$skill_dir" "$dest"
  echo "  $skill_name — installed"
done

echo ""
echo "Done. Skills available in ~/.claude/skills/:"
ls "$SKILLS_DEST"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# guardrails/install.sh — installs the pre-commit, pre-push and post-commit hooks
# from this folder into the current repo's .git/hooks/. Idempotent: re-running just
# overwrites with whatever is currently in guardrails/, no duplication and no error
# if already installed.
#
# post-commit (ROADMAP row 572) carries no gate of its own — it only re-arms the
# concurrent-edit fence on the session's own successful commit, when the fence is
# already armed. Installing it does NOT arm the fence itself — that stays opt-in
# (see guardrails/fence-refresh.sh and guardrails/README.md).

set -euo pipefail

GUARDRAILS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(git -C "$GUARDRAILS_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
# Worktree-aware: a linked worktree's hooks live in the MAIN checkout's common git dir, not in a
# per-worktree .git/hooks (a worktree's .git is a file, not a directory, pointing at the common
# one) — `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves the real, shared hooks directory either way,
# the same resolver guardrails/check-config-health.sh already uses for the same reason.
HOOKS_DIR="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --git-path hooks)"
case "$HOOKS_DIR" in
  /*) : ;;
  *) HOOKS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/$HOOKS_DIR" ;;
esac

if [ ! -d "$HOOKS_DIR" ]; then
  echo "No .git/hooks directory found at $HOOKS_DIR — is $REPO_ROOT a git repo?"
  exit 1
fi

for hook in pre-commit pre-push post-commit; do
  cp "$GUARDRAILS_DIR/$hook" "$HOOKS_DIR/$hook"
  chmod +x "$HOOKS_DIR/$hook"
  echo "Installed $hook -> $HOOKS_DIR/$hook"
done

echo "Done. The fence (pre-commit) stays OFF until a session runs guardrails/fence-refresh.sh."

=== guardrails/pre-commit ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-commit — the concurrent-edit fence (SPEC INV-11).
#
# OPT-IN by design: a session arms the fence by running guardrails/fence-refresh.sh,
# which writes the HEAD sha it last saw into .live-spec-fence (untracked, repo root),
# plus its own session token on line 2 (ROADMAP row 572 — see guardrails/post-commit).
#
# If .live-spec-fence is ABSENT, this hook passes silently — the fence is not armed,
# and that is deliberate, not a bug to "fix". If present and HEAD has moved since it
# was recorded, another writer touched the repo; the commit is blocked until the
# fence is reviewed and refreshed.
#
# This check only ever compares the recorded sha (line 1) to HEAD — it has no notion
# of sessions itself. The session's own commits stop needing a manual refresh between
# them because guardrails/post-commit re-arms the fence right after a commit that was
# made by the session that currently owns the arm (row 572); a commit from a session
# that doesn't own the arm still leaves the fence stale, so this check still blocks
# the next commit, from anyone, exactly as before.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
FENCE_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/.live-spec-fence"

# INV-24 second arm (row 104): no staged line stamps today with a future time.
if [ -x "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-future-times.sh" ]; then
  "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-future-times.sh" || exit 1
fi

# INV-152 net: a parked-for-the-human item in the resume file or a decision page must
# name its human-only fact (taste / policy / irreversible / device-feel), else it is
# the seat's to do. Scans NEXT_STEPS.md and any docs/decisions/*.md.
if [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-deferral-marker.py" ]; then
  deferral_targets=""
  [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/NEXT_STEPS.md" ] && deferral_targets="$REPO_ROOT/NEXT_STEPS.md"
  for d in "$REPO_ROOT"/docs/decisions/*.md; do
    [ -f "$d" ] && deferral_targets="$deferral_targets $d"
  done
  if [ -n "$deferral_targets" ]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    python3 "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-deferral-marker.py" $deferral_targets || exit 1
  fi
fi

# INV-175 second arm: on a shared index, a file both staged and carrying unstaged
# modifications at commit time is the signature of a second writer (or a forgotten
# re-add) touching a file mid-landing. Stop, look, re-add or investigate.
overlap="$(comm -12 <(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" diff --name-only | sort -u) \
                    <(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" diff --cached --name-only | sort -u))"
if [ -n "$overlap" ]; then
  echo "COMMIT BLOCKED — staged files carry unstaged modifications (a second writer, or a forgotten re-add):"
  echo "$overlap" | sed 's/^/  /'
  echo "  Review each file (git diff <file>), then either git add it or drop the stray edit."
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -f "$FENCE_FILE" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

recorded_sha="$(sed -n '1p' "$FENCE_FILE" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
current_sha="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD)"

if [ "$recorded_sha" != "$current_sha" ]; then
  echo "COMMIT BLOCKED — the concurrent-edit fence is armed and HEAD has moved."
  echo "  Recorded HEAD: $recorded_sha"
  echo "  Current HEAD:  $current_sha"
  recorded_token="$(sed -n '2p' "$FENCE_FILE" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
  session_token="${LIVE_SPEC_SESSION_ID:-${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-}}"
  if [ -n "$recorded_token" ] && [ "$recorded_token" != "$session_token" ]; then
    # Restart-staleness diagnosis: after a session restart (new token) or a foreign
    # window's commit, the fence blocks with no hint of WHOSE arm it is. Name it.
    echo "  This arm belongs to another session (or one that has since ended) —"
    echo "  not this one. It is not necessarily something to review; it may just be stale."
  else
    echo "  Someone else committed or pulled into this repo since your session started."
  fi
  echo "  Review what changed (e.g. git log $recorded_sha..$current_sha) if needed, then"
  echo "  re-arm the fence for this session with the one command:"
  echo "    bash guardrails/fence-refresh.sh"
  exit 1
fi

# Plan-delta guard — his word of 2026-08-10 (DECISIONS.md), the one granted exception to the
# cutting campaign's rule 2. A commit that changes the campaign plan file must stage a delta
# page rooting every changed hunk. The guard stands down in a tree that has no guard script
# (scratch repos, other hosts), and stands down inside the script when the plan is not staged.
plan_guard="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.live-spec/check-plan-delta.sh"
if [ -f "$plan_guard" ]; then
  bash "$plan_guard" || exit 1
fi

exit 0
=== guardrails/pre-push ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-push — the live-spec push gate (SPEC M-6; scope grown by prover findings F7/F4;
# gate e added for INV-17, the prototype fence).
# Blocks a push unless every gate below passes.
#
# Generic pattern for a host project: copy this file, then in guardrails/README.md's
# "how a host adapts" section swap in your own test command and prover cadence — the
# gate shape (fresh review record / green tests / ownership / coverage) travels as-is.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"
GUARDRAILS="$REPO_ROOT/guardrails"

# -- deletion-only stand-down (SPEC INV-290, ROADMAP row 502) --
# git feeds this hook one ref-update line per pushed ref on stdin (githooks(5)); read it ONCE, here,
# before any gate below can touch stdin — a manual invocation for testing leaves stdin as a tty and
# must never block on a read. A push whose every fed line deletes its remote counterpart (the
# all-zero local object id) carries no content for any gate to judge, so the whole chain stands down
# by name instead of falling to the reach map's conservative FULL — the fix for the 2026-07-27 hang
# (four tag deletions read as an empty diff, fell to the full suite, died on the two-minute limit).
# This check carries no gate letter: it is a triage read ahead of the chain, the placement
# check-push-reach.sh already holds inside gate b, not a net that blocks on red.
#
# The marker below is the machine-readable half of the convention guardrails/check-prover-record.sh
# states in full: every arm that can let a push past the prover-record demand carries one
# `# STAND-DOWN: <name>` line, and PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226 criterion 6 must name that same <name>.
# tests/test_deletion_only_push.py reads both directions off these markers.
# STAND-DOWN: deletion-only
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  PUSH_REF_LINES=""
else
  PUSH_REF_LINES="$(cat)"
fi
export PUSH_REF_LINES
if [ -n "$PUSH_REF_LINES" ]; then
  set +e
  del_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-deletion-only-push.sh")"
  del_code=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$del_code" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "$del_out"
    echo "PUSH ALLOWED — deletion-only push: standing the full gate chain down (reason: a deletion carries no content for any gate to judge, SPEC INV-290); whatever would guard the deletion itself is unaffected, since no such gate exists in this chain today."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

fail=0

# -- the fast local chain (2026-08-18) --
# The local chain runs the checks that take seconds: the prover record, the pins, skill
# loadability, and the registry and accounting checks. The one slow member is gate b, the whole
# pytest suite, which takes over twenty minutes on this machine and is the SERVER's job — the
# gates workflow runs `python3 -m pytest -q` on every push, in the step named
# "test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)" (.github/workflows/gates.yml). Running
# it a second time on the pusher's machine bought a slower push, not a safer one.
# The old chain is still here and still reachable: LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 runs gate b locally
# exactly as before, reach-scoped, with its suite-budget arm. That is the flag for a machine with
# no server, a network-less push, or anyone who wants the old behaviour.
# Nothing else moved: every gate whose value is catching something BEFORE the push — gate a's
# fresh prover record above all — runs on every push as it always did.
PUSH_FULL="${LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL:-}"

# Gate g, pin drift, is the second cost in the local chain: 56 seconds on 2026-08-18, more than
# every other fast gate together. It stays — it holds pins repaired BEFORE a push, and it proved
# sixty-odd re-aimed pins the evening before — but it stops charging a push that cannot have moved
# a pin. A pin lives in ARCHITECTURE.md or in the r5 rule-price page, and points at a file. So a
# diff touching none of: ARCHITECTURE.md, .live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md, skills/ (the r5
# page pins skill rules), the gate's own two readers, or any file an ARCHITECTURE.md pin names,
# cannot have moved one.
# The diff base is the chain's own, LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE with origin/main as the default, the base
# gate a and the reach classifier already read. Every unreadable answer runs the gate: no base, no
# diff, no pin list. The SERVER runs gate g unconditionally (.github/workflows/gates.yml), so the
# guarantee is unchanged — it just stops being paid for on every push that cannot touch it.
# PIN_REACH_FILES replaces the diff for tests only, the way REACH_FILES does in check-push-reach.sh.
gate_g_can_skip() {
  # exit 0 = this diff cannot have moved a pin, gate g may stand down; 1 = run it.
  local base changed targets f
  [ -n "$PUSH_FULL" ] && return 1
  if [ -n "${PIN_REACH_FILES:-}" ]; then
    changed="$PIN_REACH_FILES"
  else
    base="${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE:-origin/main}"
    git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base" >/dev/null || return 1
    changed="$(git diff --name-only "$base"..HEAD || true)"
  fi
  [ -z "$changed" ] && return 1
  targets="$(python3 "$GUARDRAILS/archformat.py" --pins "$REPO_ROOT/ARCHITECTURE.md" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1 | sort -u || true)"
  [ -z "$targets" ] && return 1
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    [ -z "$f" ] && continue
    case "$f" in
      ARCHITECTURE.md|.live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md|skills/*) return 1 ;;
      guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh|guardrails/archformat.py) return 1 ;;  # the gate's own reading changed
    esac
    if printf '%s\n' "$targets" | grep -qxF -- "$f"; then
      return 1
    fi
  done <<< "$changed"
  return 0
}

echo "== live-spec push gate =="

echo ""
echo "-- reach classification (one read, feeds gates a and b, SPEC INV-45) --"
set +e
reach_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-push-reach.sh")"
reach_code=$?
set -e
echo "$reach_out"

echo ""
echo "-- gate a: fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304) --"
# The reach verdict does not scope this gate (the 2718c69 stand-down, reverted on the owner's
# 2026-08-15 word). A prose-only or scoped diff still sends commits, and the record this gate
# demands is the adversarial read of the pushed RANGE (INV-304) — a thing no file-class verdict
# can stand down for. The only stand-downs that exist are the two PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226.6 names
# by hand: a deletion-only push (handled above, before this chain) and the recordless class.
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prover-record.sh" --push; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate b: test suite green (scoped by the diff's reach, SPEC INV-45) --"
if [ -z "$PUSH_FULL" ]; then
  echo "   the server runs this one: .github/workflows/gates.yml runs python3 -m pytest -q on every"
  echo "   push, in its step \"test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)\". The local"
  echo "   chain is the fast set, so a push here does not pay the suite's twenty minutes twice."
  echo "   Run it locally with LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 git push, or python3 -m pytest -q by hand."
else
  echo "   LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL is set: running the suite locally, reach-scoped, as the chain always did."
  case "$reach_code" in
    0)
      echo "   prose-only diff: the suite stands down by name; every other gate still runs."
      ;;
    2)
      scoped_files="$(printf '%s\n' "$reach_out" | sed -n 's/^SCOPED //p')"
      if ! SCOPED_TEST_FILES="$scoped_files" "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
        fail=1
      fi
      ;;
    *)
      if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
        fail=1
      fi
      ;;
  esac
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate c: every spec anchor owned by exactly one architecture node --"
echo "   Covered by gate b: tests/test_traceability.py already asserts this"
echo "   (test_architecture_owns_every_anchor_once) — no separate check needed here."

echo ""
echo "-- gate d: TEST_MATRIX.md generated Reference agrees with the body (SPEC INV-273/INV-218) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-matrix-reference.py" "$REPO_ROOT/TEST_MATRIX.md" "$REPO_ROOT/TEST_MATRIX.index.md"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate g: pin drift --"
if gate_g_can_skip; then
  echo "   the diff touches no pin: it changes neither ARCHITECTURE.md, nor the r5 rule-price page,"
  echo "   nor skills/, nor any file a pin names, so nothing in it can have moved a pin. The server"
  echo "   runs gate g on every push (.github/workflows/gates.yml), and LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 runs it here."
else
  if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-pin-drift.sh"; then
    fail=1
  fi
fi

echo "-- gate f: skill loadability --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-skill-loadability.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate e: prototype fence --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prototype-fence.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate i: shipped-language (no owner name or stray Cyrillic in the shipped set, SPEC INV-120) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-shipped-language.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate j: no broad browser-kill (cleanup targets the test resource only, SPEC INV-162) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-broad-kill.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate l: muted browser launch (every browser-driving script launches muted, SPEC INV-157) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-muted-launch.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate o: cleanup notice (every cleanup path that ends a process says what it ended, SPEC INV-204) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-cleanup-notice.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate p: touchpoint kind (a surface speaks only the kind its touchpoint affords, SPEC INV-205) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-touchpoint-kind.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# post-commit — the concurrent-edit fence's self re-arm (SPEC INV-11, ROADMAP row 572).
#
# The fence (pre-commit) blocks a commit when HEAD has moved since it was armed,
# regardless of who moved it — right when a foreign session commits, wrong when the
# session's OWN prior commit is what moved it: every commit after the first in one
# session then read as a foreign move, and the fence demanded a manual
# guardrails/fence-refresh.sh each time (PROBLEMS.md, 2026-07-27 / 2026-08-07).
#
# This hook re-arms the fence on the session's own successful commit ONLY. The fence
# file (.live-spec-fence) carries the armed sha on line 1 and, since row 572, the
# arming session's token on line 2 (from $LIVE_SPEC_SESSION_ID if set, else
# $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, else empty — empty means no token, which means no
# auto-rearm: the historical manual-refresh-only behavior). A commit re-arms the
# fence to its own new HEAD only when its own session token is non-empty AND matches
# the token already recorded — i.e. only the session that currently owns the arm can
# extend it.
#
# Token-matching alone is not enough (adversarial review, row 572 defect D1): a
# session that commits with `--no-verify` skips pre-commit — the staleness check
# never runs — but post-commit still fires. If a foreign commit had slid in first
# (fence goes stale at the recorded sha, foreign commit lands because a first writer
# through an armed-but-unmoved HEAD is allowed), the `--no-verify` commit's token
# still matches the recorded one, and a token-only check would re-arm the fence to a
# HEAD that CONTAINS the foreign commit — silently absorbing it, with nobody ever
# shown that a foreign move happened.
#
# So this hook also requires that the new HEAD's PARENT (`git rev-parse HEAD^`)
# equals the sha recorded on line 1 — i.e. this commit's own parent is exactly what
# the fence last saw, so nothing landed in between. If it does not (a foreign commit
# slid in, or the session amended and rewrote history out from under its own arm),
# the hook leaves the fence file untouched: the recorded sha stays stale, and the
# fence still blocks at the next honest (non-`--no-verify`) commit, from anyone.
#
# Accepted price: this makes a session's own `git commit --amend` cost one manual
# guardrails/fence-refresh.sh afterward. An amend rewrites the very commit the fence
# had recorded on line 1 into a new sha; the amended commit's parent is its
# grandparent, not the recorded (now-superseded) sha, so the parent check correctly
# reads this as "something changed underneath the arm" and refuses to auto-rearm.
# That one manual step per amend is the deliberate cost of closing D1.
#
# A foreign session's commit still lands (the fence only ever catches DIVERGENCE,
# never the first writer through an armed-but-unmoved HEAD — that is unchanged and
# is not this hook's job to alter). But that foreign commit's token does not match
# what is recorded, so this hook leaves the fence file untouched: the recorded sha
# goes stale, and the very next commit by ANYONE finds HEAD has moved past it and
# blocks — the fence keeps its teeth against another window.
#
# If the fence is not armed (no .live-spec-fence), this hook is a no-op: it never
# arms the fence on its own — the fence stays opt-in, via guardrails/fence-refresh.sh.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
FENCE_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/.live-spec-fence"

[ -f "$FENCE_FILE" ] || exit 0

recorded_sha="$(sed -n '1p' "$FENCE_FILE" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
recorded_token="$(sed -n '2p' "$FENCE_FILE" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
session_token="${LIVE_SPEC_SESSION_ID:-${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-}}"

# No session token available (plain shell, no Claude session, no override) — never
# auto-rearm; guardrails/fence-refresh.sh remains the only way, same as before this fix.
[ -n "$session_token" ] || exit 0

# Only the session that currently owns the arm gets to extend it.
[ "$recorded_token" = "$session_token" ] || exit 0

# D1: token match alone is not proof nothing landed in between (a --no-verify commit
# skips the pre-commit staleness check entirely). Require this commit's own parent
# to be exactly the sha the fence last recorded — if a foreign commit slid in, or an
# amend rewrote the recorded commit out from under the arm, HEAD^ will not match and
# this hook must leave the fence alone.
new_head_parent="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD^ 2>/dev/null || true)"
[ -n "$new_head_parent" ] && [ "$new_head_parent" = "$recorded_sha" ] || exit 0

new_head="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD)"
{
  echo "$new_head"
  echo "$session_token"
} > "$FENCE_FILE"

exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-commit — the concurrent-edit fence (SPEC INV-11).
#
# OPT-IN by design: a session arms the fence by running guardrails/fence-refresh.sh,
# which writes the HEAD sha it last saw into .live-spec-fence (untracked, repo root),
# plus its own session token on line 2 (ROADMAP row 572 — see guardrails/post-commit).
#
# If .live-spec-fence is ABSENT, this hook passes silently — the fence is not armed,
# and that is deliberate, not a bug to "fix". If present and HEAD has moved since it
# was recorded, another writer touched the repo; the commit is blocked until the
# fence is reviewed and refreshed.
#
# This check only ever compares the recorded sha (line 1) to HEAD — it has no notion
# of sessions itself. The session's own commits stop needing a manual refresh between
# them because guardrails/post-commit re-arms the fence right after a commit that was
# made by the session that currently owns the arm (row 572); a commit from a session
# that doesn't own the arm still leaves the fence stale, so this check still blocks
# the next commit, from anyone, exactly as before.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
FENCE_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/.live-spec-fence"

# INV-24 second arm (row 104): no staged line stamps today with a future time.
if [ -x "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-future-times.sh" ]; then
  "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-future-times.sh" || exit 1
fi

# INV-152 net: a parked-for-the-human item in the resume file or a decision page must
# name its human-only fact (taste / policy / irreversible / device-feel), else it is
# the seat's to do. Scans NEXT_STEPS.md and any docs/decisions/*.md.
if [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-deferral-marker.py" ]; then
  deferral_targets=""
  [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/NEXT_STEPS.md" ] && deferral_targets="$REPO_ROOT/NEXT_STEPS.md"
  for d in "$REPO_ROOT"/docs/decisions/*.md; do
    [ -f "$d" ] && deferral_targets="$deferral_targets $d"
  done
  if [ -n "$deferral_targets" ]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    python3 "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-deferral-marker.py" $deferral_targets || exit 1
  fi
fi

# INV-175 second arm: on a shared index, a file both staged and carrying unstaged
# modifications at commit time is the signature of a second writer (or a forgotten
# re-add) touching a file mid-landing. Stop, look, re-add or investigate.
overlap="$(comm -12 <(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" diff --name-only | sort -u) \
                    <(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" diff --cached --name-only | sort -u))"
if [ -n "$overlap" ]; then
  echo "COMMIT BLOCKED — staged files carry unstaged modifications (a second writer, or a forgotten re-add):"
  echo "$overlap" | sed 's/^/  /'
  echo "  Review each file (git diff <file>), then either git add it or drop the stray edit."
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -f "$FENCE_FILE" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

recorded_sha="$(sed -n '1p' "$FENCE_FILE" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
current_sha="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD)"

if [ "$recorded_sha" != "$current_sha" ]; then
  echo "COMMIT BLOCKED — the concurrent-edit fence is armed and HEAD has moved."
  echo "  Recorded HEAD: $recorded_sha"
  echo "  Current HEAD:  $current_sha"
  recorded_token="$(sed -n '2p' "$FENCE_FILE" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
  session_token="${LIVE_SPEC_SESSION_ID:-${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-}}"
  if [ -n "$recorded_token" ] && [ "$recorded_token" != "$session_token" ]; then
    # Restart-staleness diagnosis: after a session restart (new token) or a foreign
    # window's commit, the fence blocks with no hint of WHOSE arm it is. Name it.
    echo "  This arm belongs to another session (or one that has since ended) —"
    echo "  not this one. It is not necessarily something to review; it may just be stale."
  else
    echo "  Someone else committed or pulled into this repo since your session started."
  fi
  echo "  Review what changed (e.g. git log $recorded_sha..$current_sha) if needed, then"
  echo "  re-arm the fence for this session with the one command:"
  echo "    bash guardrails/fence-refresh.sh"
  exit 1
fi

# Plan-delta guard — his word of 2026-08-10 (DECISIONS.md), the one granted exception to the
# cutting campaign's rule 2. A commit that changes the campaign plan file must stage a delta
# page rooting every changed hunk. The guard stands down in a tree that has no guard script
# (scratch repos, other hosts), and stands down inside the script when the plan is not staged.
plan_guard="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.live-spec/check-plan-delta.sh"
if [ -f "$plan_guard" ]; then
  bash "$plan_guard" || exit 1
fi

exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-push — the live-spec push gate (SPEC M-6; scope grown by prover findings F7/F4;
# gate e added for INV-17, the prototype fence).
# Blocks a push unless every gate below passes.
#
# Generic pattern for a host project: copy this file, then in guardrails/README.md's
# "how a host adapts" section swap in your own test command and prover cadence — the
# gate shape (fresh review record / green tests / ownership / coverage) travels as-is.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"
GUARDRAILS="$REPO_ROOT/guardrails"

# -- deletion-only stand-down (SPEC INV-290, ROADMAP row 502) --
# git feeds this hook one ref-update line per pushed ref on stdin (githooks(5)); read it ONCE, here,
# before any gate below can touch stdin — a manual invocation for testing leaves stdin as a tty and
# must never block on a read. A push whose every fed line deletes its remote counterpart (the
# all-zero local object id) carries no content for any gate to judge, so the whole chain stands down
# by name instead of falling to the reach map's conservative FULL — the fix for the 2026-07-27 hang
# (four tag deletions read as an empty diff, fell to the full suite, died on the two-minute limit).
# This check carries no gate letter: it is a triage read ahead of the chain, the placement
# check-push-reach.sh already holds inside gate b, not a net that blocks on red.
#
# The marker below is the machine-readable half of the convention guardrails/check-prover-record.sh
# states in full: every arm that can let a push past the prover-record demand carries one
# `# STAND-DOWN: <name>` line, and PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226 criterion 6 must name that same <name>.
# tests/test_deletion_only_push.py reads both directions off these markers.
# STAND-DOWN: deletion-only
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  PUSH_REF_LINES=""
else
  PUSH_REF_LINES="$(cat)"
fi
export PUSH_REF_LINES
if [ -n "$PUSH_REF_LINES" ]; then
  set +e
  del_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-deletion-only-push.sh")"
  del_code=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$del_code" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "$del_out"
    echo "PUSH ALLOWED — deletion-only push: standing the full gate chain down (reason: a deletion carries no content for any gate to judge, SPEC INV-290); whatever would guard the deletion itself is unaffected, since no such gate exists in this chain today."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

fail=0

# -- the fast local chain (2026-08-18) --
# The local chain runs the checks that take seconds: the prover record, the pins, skill
# loadability, and the registry and accounting checks. The one slow member is gate b, the whole
# pytest suite, which takes over twenty minutes on this machine and is the SERVER's job — the
# gates workflow runs `python3 -m pytest -q` on every push, in the step named
# "test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)" (.github/workflows/gates.yml). Running
# it a second time on the pusher's machine bought a slower push, not a safer one.
# The old chain is still here and still reachable: LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 runs gate b locally
# exactly as before, reach-scoped, with its suite-budget arm. That is the flag for a machine with
# no server, a network-less push, or anyone who wants the old behaviour.
# Nothing else moved: every gate whose value is catching something BEFORE the push — gate a's
# fresh prover record above all — runs on every push as it always did.
PUSH_FULL="${LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL:-}"

# every other fast gate together. It stays — it holds pins repaired BEFORE a push, and it proved

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# post-commit — the concurrent-edit fence's self re-arm (SPEC INV-11, ROADMAP row 572).
#
# The fence (pre-commit) blocks a commit when HEAD has moved since it was armed,
# regardless of who moved it — right when a foreign session commits, wrong when the
# session's OWN prior commit is what moved it: every commit after the first in one
# session then read as a foreign move, and the fence demanded a manual
# guardrails/fence-refresh.sh each time (PROBLEMS.md, 2026-07-27 / 2026-08-07).
#
# This hook re-arms the fence on the session's own successful commit ONLY. The fence
# file (.live-spec-fence) carries the armed sha on line 1 and, since row 572, the
# arming session's token on line 2 (from $LIVE_SPEC_SESSION_ID if set, else
# $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, else empty — empty means no token, which means no
# auto-rearm: the historical manual-refresh-only behavior). A commit re-arms the
# fence to its own new HEAD only when its own session token is non-empty AND matches
# the token already recorded — i.e. only the session that currently owns the arm can
# extend it.
#
# Token-matching alone is not enough (adversarial review, row 572 defect D1): a
# session that commits with `--no-verify` skips pre-commit — the staleness check
# never runs — but post-commit still fires. If a foreign commit had slid in first
# (fence goes stale at the recorded sha, foreign commit lands because a first writer
# through an armed-but-unmoved HEAD is allowed), the `--no-verify` commit's token
# still matches the recorded one, and a token-only check would re-arm the fence to a
# HEAD that CONTAINS the foreign commit — silently absorbing it, with nobody ever
# shown that a foreign move happened.
#
# So this hook also requires that the new HEAD's PARENT (`git rev-parse HEAD^`)
# equals the sha recorded on line 1 — i.e. this commit's own parent is exactly what
# the fence last saw, so nothing landed in between. If it does not (a foreign commit
# slid in, or the session amended and rewrote history out from under its own arm),
# the hook leaves the fence file untouched: the recorded sha stays stale, and the
# fence still blocks at the next honest (non-`--no-verify`) commit, from anyone.
#
# Accepted price: this makes a session's own `git commit --amend` cost one manual
# guardrails/fence-refresh.sh afterward. An amend rewrites the very commit the fence
# had recorded on line 1 into a new sha; the amended commit's parent is its
# grandparent, not the recorded (now-superseded) sha, so the parent check correctly
# reads this as "something changed underneath the arm" and refuses to auto-rearm.
# That one manual step per amend is the deliberate cost of closing D1.
#
# A foreign session's commit still lands (the fence only ever catches DIVERGENCE,
# never the first writer through an armed-but-unmoved HEAD — that is unchanged and
# is not this hook's job to alter). But that foreign commit's token does not match
# what is recorded, so this hook leaves the fence file untouched: the recorded sha
# goes stale, and the very next commit by ANYONE finds HEAD has moved past it and
# blocks — the fence keeps its teeth against another window.
#
# If the fence is not armed (no .live-spec-fence), this hook is a no-op: it never
# arms the fence on its own — the fence stays opt-in, via guardrails/fence-refresh.sh.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
FENCE_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/.live-spec-fence"

[ -f "$FENCE_FILE" ] || exit 0

recorded_sha="$(sed -n '1p' "$FENCE_FILE" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
recorded_token="$(sed -n '2p' "$FENCE_FILE" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
session_token="${LIVE_SPEC_SESSION_ID:-${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-}}"

# No session token available (plain shell, no Claude session, no override) — never
# auto-rearm; guardrails/fence-refresh.sh remains the only way, same as before this fix.
[ -n "$session_token" ] || exit 0

# Only the session that currently owns the arm gets to extend it.
[ "$recorded_token" = "$session_token" ] || exit 0

# D1: token match alone is not proof nothing landed in between (a --no-verify commit
# skips the pre-commit staleness check entirely). Require this commit's own parent
# to be exactly the sha the fence last recorded — if a foreign commit slid in, or an
# amend rewrote the recorded commit out from under the arm, HEAD^ will not match and
# this hook must leave the fence alone.
new_head_parent="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD^ 2>/dev/null || true)"
[ -n "$new_head_parent" ] && [ "$new_head_parent" = "$recorded_sha" ] || exit 0

new_head="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD)"
{
  echo "$new_head"
  echo "$session_token"
} > "$FENCE_FILE"

exit 0

# gates.yml — the CI mirror of the push gate (SPEC M-5, ROADMAP row 14).

name: gates
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: "install pytest"
        run: pip install pytest pyyaml
      # The external canon, pinned. Before this step existed the suite ran with no clone,
      # so every assertion that reads the externalized product-prover skipped on every CI
      # run forever, and CI claimed a green it had not earned (ROADMAP row 622 territory;
      # the same fork the emergency branch reached from the other side). The pack now
      # INSTALLS the canon rather than pretending to prove it: --ref names the exact commit
      # the pack's assertions are written against, and --expect-commit verifies the checkout
      # landed there, so a moved tag or branch cannot change what CI proves. Moving the pin
      # is a deliberate pack change; tests/test_prover_adapter_contract.py holds its shape.
      - name: "install the external product-prover canon (pinned, gate b's evidence)"
        run: >-
          scripts/install-external-skills.sh
          --ref 540914d740e4f6178d1a69f324c43a0ae871e066
          --expect-commit 540914d740e4f6178d1a69f324c43a0ae871e066
      - name: "test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 -m pytest -q
      - name: "gate a — fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        # LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE lets the script judge the inbox-only carve-out (row 269,
        # SPEC M-6/INV-112): a push whose diff is exactly one new inbox/ file owes no
        # fresh record. The same base carries the range arm, which reads the pushed delta
        # against the state the remote already holds. github.event.before is the pre-push
        # SHA on a push; on a PR it is empty and the script falls back to origin/main,
        # which the fetch-depth-0 checkout above carries.
        env:
          LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: guardrails/check-prover-record.sh --push
      - name: "gate d — TEST_MATRIX.md generated Reference agrees with the body (SPEC INV-273/INV-218)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-matrix-reference.py TEST_MATRIX.md TEST_MATRIX.index.md

        run: guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh

        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-skill-loadability.sh
      - name: "gate e — prototype fence"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-prototype-fence.sh
      - name: "gate i — shipped-language (no owner name or stray Cyrillic in the shipped set, SPEC INV-120)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-shipped-language.sh

        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-broad-kill.sh
      - name: "gate l — muted browser launch (every browser-driving script launches muted, SPEC INV-157)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-muted-launch.sh
      - name: "gate o — cleanup notice (every cleanup path that ends a process says what it ended, SPEC INV-204)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-cleanup-notice.sh
      - name: "gate p — touchpoint kind (a surface speaks only the kind its touchpoint affords, SPEC INV-205)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}

        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        # LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE lets the gate read the push range (the same base as gate a); on a PR it
        # is empty and the gate falls back to origin/main.
        env:
          LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: guardrails/check-skill-review.sh

        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}

      # need no separate CI step here and no ci-mirror carve-out — a suite-riding check carries no gate
      # letter for the mirror to track.

        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-ci-mirror.sh
      - name: "gate w — every gate can fail (every gate in this chain carries a known-red proof, SPEC INV-212)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-every-gate-can-fail.py
      - name: "gate x — generated index (the committed index equals a fresh build off the body; body and index agree; an empty body reds by name, SPEC INV-258/INV-259/INV-218)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-index-generated.py PRODUCT_SPEC.md PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md
      - name: "gate y — agent card (a live-spec host tree carries its .live-spec/agent.md card, SPEC INV-219)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-agent-card.py
      - name: "gate aa — doc findings bound (no live document above its recorded finding count; a cleared document stays at zero, SPEC INV-301)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}

        env:
          LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-doc-findings-bound.py
      - name: "gate ad — published tree counts (every count this repository publishes about its own tree matches the tree, and the reproduction command beside it returns the published number, SPEC INV-305)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-tree-counts.py
      - name: "gate ae — named checks (the registry says what each runnable file a skill body names is, SPEC INV-306)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-named-checks.py
      - name: "gate af — gate device manifest (guardrails/gates-manifest.json joins every gate's script, red proof and CI-mirror status from pre-push, gate-red-proofs.json and ci-mirror.json; it reds where a fresh build differs from the committed file, or where a gates.yml step's law sentence differs from the gate's own, SPEC INV-210/INV-212)"

=== stranger-monitor.yml ===
# stranger-monitor.yml — the package repo's scheduled stranger-door monitor (SPEC INV-148, INV-147).
# The schedule INV-147 requires, realized for this repo: it wakes the monitor on a daily cron (and on a
# manual dispatch for a verify hand-run), runs scripts/stranger-wish-monitor.py once, and pushes any inbox
# file the monitor committed. Single instance by the concurrency group — a second scheduled run waits for
# the in-flight one rather than racing its push (the CI form of the per-host lock the monitor keeps for a
# host that runs the script directly, SPEC INV-147). It commits and pushes under the action's own token as
# github-actions[bot]; the push carries inbox commits only, riding the inbox-only push-gate carve-out
# (SPEC M-6, INV-112). A GITHUB_TOKEN push does not re-trigger the gates workflow, which is correct for an
# inbox deposit awaiting the next session's sweep.
name: stranger-monitor
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 6 * * *"   # daily at 06:17 UTC — an off-the-hour minute keeps clear of the top-of-hour crowd
  workflow_dispatch:        # a manual hand-run, the verify path (SPEC INV-148 / M-290)

# serialize runs: a second scheduled run waits for the in-flight one instead of cancelling it, so two runs
# never overlap and race the push. cancel-in-progress stays false by intent (SPEC INV-148).
concurrency:
  group: stranger-monitor
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # push the inbox commit the monitor makes
  issues: write          # record the surfaced-generation marker comment on an Issue (SPEC INV-146)
  discussions: write     # record it on a Discussion (SPEC INV-146)

jobs:
  monitor:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0    # the push step compares HEAD against origin to find the monitor's commit
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: identify the committer
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
      - name: run the monitor
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}   # gh reads the token for `issue`/`api graphql`/`repo view`
        run: python3 scripts/stranger-wish-monitor.py
      - name: push any bridged inbox commit
        run: |
          # The monitor commits touching inbox/ only; push whatever it landed. A no-op run (no open
          # stranger item) leaves nothing to push and exits clean. A rebase absorbs any commit main took
          # since checkout, so the inbox commit lands without overwriting other work.
          if [ -z "$(git log "origin/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}..HEAD" --oneline)" ]; then
            echo "no bridged commit this run — nothing to push"
            exit 0
          fi
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if git pull --rebase origin "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" && git push origin "HEAD:${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"; then
              echo "pushed the bridged inbox commit"
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "push attempt ${attempt} failed; retrying after rebase"
          done
          echo "could not push the bridged inbox commit after retries" >&2
          exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stop-hook: catch empty affirmation / validation aimed at the user in outgoing chat.

A reply carries no line telling the human he is right, praising his question or his intuition, or
framing the agent's own work as superior ("measured, not guessed"; "honest, not on the eye"). Empty
validation costs the reader attention and returns nothing; the reply owes the finding or the action,
and nothing else leads. The exchange that set this standing is dated in JOURNAL.md. This is the machine
behind the personal profile's no-affirmation rule, a sibling of the scissors scan.

Two tiers. The UNIVERSAL tier holds the language-neutral English validation phrases. A host's own extra
patterns — another language, a narrower personal phrase — load from an optional overlay file
`~/.claude/hooks/affirmation-personal.json` (a JSON list of regex strings), owned by the personal layer;
this file never creates or edits that overlay. Missing or malformed overlay falls back to universal-only,
silently.

Reads every assistant message shown since the last human turn (hooks/turn_reader.py), so an affirmation
in an early narration line reds like one in the final reply — the reach its siblings took at the row-482
fix and this arm had missed until 2026-07-27. A phrase demonstrated inside «guillemets», "double
quotes", or `backticks`, and any line inside a fenced ``` code block, is stripped before matching — so
quoting a banned phrase to talk ABOUT it is not itself a live instance. A surviving match BLOCKS the stop
with a rewrite instruction.
"""

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stop-hook: an internal code may only trail a sentence as a quiet anchor (SPEC INV-28, base rule 2).

The law says every human-facing sentence stands on its own in the product's words, and internal handles
— a queue row number, an INV/M/E/T code — trail in parentheses for anyone who wants to follow them. A
sentence that leads with a handle hands the reader a number he has no way to resolve.

It decayed for want of a machine. On 2026-07-27 the human was handed "rows 386 and 412, hanging since 18
July" and answered plainly: he does not remember row numbers, the sentence tells him nothing, put a hook
on it. This is that hook.

WHAT IT READS. Every assistant message shown since the last human turn (hooks/turn_reader.py), so a
naked code in an early narration line reds like one in the final reply.

WHAT PASSES, by construction:
  - a code inside parentheses or square brackets — the lawful trailing anchor; the span is now allowed
    to carry one embedded line break, so an anchor broken across a line by wrapping still clears;
  - a table row (a line starting with `|`), where the neighbouring cell carries the plain words;
  - a fenced code block, an inline `backtick` span, and a «quoted» or "quoted" span — text ABOUT a code
    rather than a code addressed to the reader;
  - a bare number with no code word in front of it, since this net reads the naming, not arithmetic;
  - the Russian naming word plus a number when the same line goes on to name a file — either the word
    for "file" in any inflection, or a filename-shaped token (word.ext) — since that is a line inside a
    source file, which owes no anchor.

WHAT NOW ALSO REDS, this repository's own citation idioms that the first cut of the net missed:
  - a document name run directly against its number — "ROADMAP 480", "ARCHITECTURE 122",
    "PRODUCT_SPEC 352", "TEST_MATRIX 6" — the same naked-code shape as "row 480" one word earlier;
  - the multi-letter codes (INV, ROW, ACT) read aloud with a space instead of the inline dash —
    "INV 281" reds exactly as "INV-281" does; the single-letter codes (M, E, T, S, D, A, B, C, F, R)

########## check-prover-record.sh ##########
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-prover-record.sh — gate (a) of the push gate: a fresh, committed prover record
# dated today must exist before a push, and that record must be fresh for BOTH guarded
# documents — PRODUCT_SPEC.md and ARCHITECTURE.md (SPEC M-6, INV-116: every live-spec push
# is preceded by a fresh re-check recorded in docs/prover/, covering the spec and the
# architecture alike).
#
# ONE RECORD PER PUSH (SPEC INV-304). A push once owed two review records to two separate
# gates: this one, and a second adversarial read of the pushed delta kept in its own home.
# The two are one pass, so they are one record. On the PUSH road this gate therefore also
# holds what the second gate held: the record names the pushed range, carries the fields
# that say what the review covered, and leaves no blocking finding open.
#
# THE LAW behind that half. A change that passes every test can still be wrong in ways no
# test asks about. A reviewer briefed to find reasons to refuse the change reads it
# differently from a reviewer set on confirming it, and the difference is what the suite
# misses. So the record a push carries is an adversarial read of the very commits it sends.
#

########## check-push-reach.sh ##########
#!/usr/bin/env bash

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-suite-budget.sh — the suite wall-time budget's mechanical net (SPEC INV-41, INV-164,
# ROADMAP row 361).
#
# ARCHITECTURE.md states a quality budget for the full suite's wall-time; nothing machine-read it
# against the real number, which is exactly how the stated budget (once ≤ 60 s) drifted silently
# behind the measured figure (~95 s) until a full prover pass caught it (2026-07-16). This gate
# closes the hole: it reads the run's own pytest tail line ("N passed in X.XXs (...)") and the
# architecture's stated budget row, and reds the moment the measured figure exceeds the stated one
# — naming BOTH numbers, so the failure is fixable on sight (speed the suite, or re-set the budget
# to the fresh measured figure) and a budget claim can never again go unread.
#
# Usage: check-suite-budget.sh <log-file> [architecture-md]
#   log-file         a captured pytest -q run's stdout/stderr (its LAST "in <float>s" tail line
#                     is read — a run may print several such lines from earlier tool output).
#   architecture-md   defaults to ARCHITECTURE.md at the repo root.

set -euo pipefail
REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

LOG="${1:-}"
ARCH="${2:-$REPO_ROOT/ARCHITECTURE.md}"

if [ -z "$LOG" ] || [ ! -f "$LOG" ]; then
  echo "FAIL (suite budget): no readable log file given ('$LOG')."
  exit 1
fi

# the LAST line matching pytest's own tail shape: "<N> passed in <float>s" (may also read
# "... in <float>s (H:MM:SS)" — only the seconds figure right after "in" is read).
measured="$(grep -oE 'in [0-9]+\.[0-9]+s' "$LOG" 2>/dev/null | tail -n1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' || true)"

if [ -z "$measured" ]; then
  echo "FAIL (suite budget): the log's duration line was unreadable — no 'in <float>s' tail found in $LOG."
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -f "$ARCH" ]; then
  echo "FAIL (suite budget): the budget row was unreadable — $ARCH not found."

# Инвентарь проверок LiveSpec — блокирующие гейты, хуки и CI

Разведка велась по `guardrails/` (150 файлов, включая фикстуры), `hooks/` (18 файлов), `.github/workflows/` (2 файла), git-хукам (`guardrails/pre-commit`, `pre-push`, `post-commit`, устанавливаемым через `guardrails/install.sh`) и вспомогательным `scaffold/guardrails/` (гейт h). Источники: сам код проверок, `guardrails/gates-manifest.json` (сгенерированный джойн всех 29 букв гейтов), `guardrails/ci-mirror.json`, `guardrails/judge-hooks.json` (какие hooks реально подключены к `~/.claude/settings.json`), и grep каждого имени файла по репозиторию.

**Важная структурная находка**: `guardrails/pre-push` — единственный оркестратор push-гейта (29 букв a…af, буквы z/ab/ac упразднены 2026-08-18). Он же **дословно мирроритcя** в `.github/workflows/gates.yml` (с 4 задекларированными исключениями в `ci-mirror.json`: c, k, m, v). `guardrails/pre-commit` — отдельный, более мелкий набор из 5 проверок. Значительная часть `guardrails/*.py` **не имеет буквы гейта** — они «едут в комплекте» с pytest-сьютом (гейт b) и вызываются только своими `tests/test_*.py`; несколько таких проверок **UNARMED** (не применяются к живому дереву, только к фикстурам, до будущей миграции формата спеки). `hooks/` почти целиком **opt-in**: `guardrails/judge-hooks.json` прямо перечисляет, что реально «wired» в `~/.claude/settings.json` по умолчанию — только `clock-hook` и `chat-law-hook` (оба — инъекция текста, не блокирующие проверки); все остальные hooks (scissors/hedge/affirmation/code-anchor scans, register-judge, conduct-judge, lean-orchestrator-scan) — библиотека/opt-in, причём 6 из них хозяин прямо «остановил» 17.08.2026 согласно комментариям в коде.

## Сводная таблица

| Файл | Когда срабатывает (доказательство) | Что проверяет | Какую реальную потерю предотвращает | Метка |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `guardrails/pre-commit` (fence-часть) | pre-commit git hook, если сессия вызвала `fence-refresh.sh` | HEAD не сдвинулся с момента «вооружения» забора | Перезапись/потеря чужих коммитов при одновременной работе двух сессий | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| `guardrails/pre-commit` (overlap-часть, инлайн) | pre-commit git hook, всегда | staged-файл не несёт ещё и unstaged-изменений | Забытый повторный `git add`/второй писатель молча теряет часть правки | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| `guardrails/check-future-times.sh` | вызывается из `pre-commit` (grep подтверждён) | добавленная строка не датирует «сегодня» временем позже момента коммита | Фабрикация несуществующего будущего времени в постоянной записи проекта | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| `guardrails/check-deferral-marker.py` | вызывается из `pre-commit` | пункт «отложено на человека» называет human-only причину | Внутренний ритуал «отложить решение»; предмет — свой же формат NEXT_STEPS/decisions | САМОРЕФЕРЕНТНО |
| `.live-spec/check-plan-delta.sh` (вне guardrails/) | вызывается из `pre-commit`, если план-файл кампании застейджен | коммит, меняющий план, несёт delta-страницу | Собственная бухгалтерия плана кампании LiveSpec | САМОРЕФЕРЕНТНО |
| `guardrails/post-commit` | post-commit git hook | нет своего гейта — только перевооружает fence при совпадении токена сессии | — (housekeeping, не проверка) | — |
| `guardrails/check-deletion-only-push.sh` | вызывается из `pre-push` до цепочки букв (grep подтверждён) | все ref-линии пуша — чистое удаление | Решает, снимать ли всю цепочку защит целиком | САМОРЕФЕРЕНТНО |
| `guardrails/check-push-reach.sh` | вызывается из `pre-push`, кормит гейты a/b | может ли диф вообще задеть python-сьют (prose/scoped/full) | От её точности зависит, запустятся ли реальные тесты (гейт b) | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| **Гейт a** `check-prover-record.sh` | pre-push + CI (`gates.yml`, шаг «gate a») | наличие свежей, датированной сегодняшним числом записи ревью PRODUCT_SPEC.md/ARCHITECTURE.md | Самозаявленная запись «я проверил» — без независимой верификации содержания; см. отдельный разбор ниже | НЕЯСНО |
| **Гейт b** `check-tests.sh` | pre-push (при `LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1`) + CI всегда | весь pytest-сьют зелёный | Регрессии реального поведения продукта | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| **Гейт c** (нет скрипта, свёрнут в b) | pre-push печатает заметку, реальная проверка — `tests/test_traceability.py` внутри сьюта | каждый spec-anchor принадлежит ровно одному узлу архитектуры | Сам pre-push прямо пишет «покрыто гейтом b, отдельной проверки нет» | ДУБЛЬ (гейта b) |
| **Гейт d** `check-matrix-reference.py` | pre-push + CI | сгенерированная Reference-таблица TEST_MATRIX.md совпадает со свежей сборкой из тела | Устаревшая/расходящаяся таблица вводит читателя в заблуждение (артефакт≠источник) | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| **Гейт e** `check-prototype-fence.sh` | pre-push + CI | prod-файл не ссылается структурно на `prototype/` | Прототип, случайно подключённый в продакшн-путь | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| **Гейт f** `check-skill-loadability.sh` | pre-push + CI | у каждого шаблона skill корректный frontmatter/описание/версия | Битый skill, который харнесс не сможет проиндексировать — реальный шипуемый артефакт | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| **Гейт g** `check-pin-drift.sh` | pre-push (условно, есть быстрый skip) + CI | построчные «пины» в ARCHITECTURE.md указывают на актуальную строку | Устаревшая ссылка в собственной документации архитектуры | САМОРЕФЕРЕНТНО |
| **Гейт h** `scaffold/guardrails/check_{completeness,tests_present,traces_to_spec,conflicts}.py` | pre-push + CI (репозиторий — «свой первый хост») | реестр шипуемых поверхностей полон; тесты присутствуют; трассировка к спеке; нет конфликтов | Это и есть реальный код продукта (шаблон guardrails, который получают usdopt-проекты) | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| **Гейт i** `check-shipped-language.sh` | pre-push + CI | в шипуемых файлах нет кириллицы/личного имени владельца | Утечка личных данных автора во внешний открытый пакет | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| **Гейт j** `check-broad-kill.sh` | pre-push + CI | cleanup завершает только доказанно свой процесс (PID/pgid), не по имени | Задокументированный реальный инцидент: `pkill chrome` убил живой браузер владельца вне git | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| **Гейт k** `check-freeze.sh` | pre-push (только если есть локальный `.spec-freeze/`) + не в CI (нет baseline) | якоря/маркеры/числа в охраняемых доках не изменились против локального снапшота | Тихая подмена смысла при «компакции» контекста — но baseline gitignored и применяется только к своим докам | САМОРЕФЕРЕНТНО |
| **Гейт l** `check-muted-launch.sh` | pre-push + CI | скрипт, запускающий headless-браузер, обязан глушить звук | Реальный инцидент: тест играл звук на машине во время прогона | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| **Гейт m** `check-config-health.sh` (+ sub-arm ниже) | pre-push (skip в CI по имени) | установленный `.git/hooks/*` побайтово совпадает с `guardrails/` | Установленный хук молча не содержит защит, которые есть в исходнике | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| `guardrails/check-config-health-perms.py` (под-рычаг m) | вызывается из `check-config-health.sh` (grep подтверждён) | путь в правиле разрешений харнесса реально существует | Реальный случай: переименованная папка → неделя молчаливо проваленных деплоев | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| **Гейт n** `check-earned-message.py` | pre-push (report-only) + CI (report-only) | депозит в inbox называет «рождение» (блокировку/находку) | Хайгиена собственного inter-agent мессенджинга | САМОРЕФЕРЕНТНО |
| **Гейт o** `check-cleanup-notice.sh` | pre-push + CI | код, завершающий процесс, где-то печатает уведомление о чём | Видимость перед потенциально опасным убийством процесса (слабее гейта j) | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| **Гейт p** `check-touchpoint-kind.py` | pre-push + CI | поверхность говорит только тем «видом» сообщения, который позволяет её touchpoint (sync/async) | Собственная таксономия каналов коммуникации агент↔человек LiveSpec | САМОРЕФЕРЕНТНО |
| **Гейт q** `check-board.py` | pre-push + CI | WAITING.md ничего не теряет: cap=12 показанных, вытеснение — только в список, не в никуда | Забытый вопрос/решение, ожидающее ответа человека, исчезает бесследно | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |
| **Гейт r** `check-authority-anchor.py` | pre-push + CI | решение, записанное «как решение человека», называет проверяемый обмен (дату) | Агент вкладывает в уста человека решение, которого тот не принимал | ЗАЩИЩАЕТ |

## «Гейты, проверяющие гейты» (мета-гварды)

Единственный предмет каждого из следующих — другая проверка, её реестр или её конфигурация, а не код продукта/данные пользователя:

- `guardrails/check-ci-mirror.sh` (гейт u) — сверяет буквы гейтов в `pre-push` с шагами `gates.yml`.
- `guardrails/check-judge-listed.py` (гейт v) — сверяет `hooks/`-подключения из `judge-hooks.json` с массивом `~/.claude/settings.json`.
- `guardrails/check-every-gate-can-fail.py` (гейт w) — требует у каждой буквы гейта known-red-proof в `gate-red-proofs.json`.
- `guardrails/check-hooks-can-fire.py` — тот же принцип, но для `hooks/`, читает `hook-red-fixtures/` и `hook-red-proofs.json`.
- `guardrails/check-named-checks.py` (гейт ae) — сверяет `scripts/check-registry.json` (описание каждого проверочного файла) с деревом.
- `guardrails/check-gates-manifest.py` (гейт af) — пересобирает `gates-manifest.json` из pre-push + `gate-red-proofs.json` + `ci-mirror.json` + `gates.yml` и сравнивает построчно, включая совпадение формулировки закона гейта в CI и в pre-push.
- `guardrails/check-tree-counts.py` (гейт ad) — включает в себя, в частности, проверку «pre-push объявляет N букв гейтов, и README называет то же N» — буквальная проверка манифеста гейтов числом.

Данные (не скрипты, но обслуживающие исключительно этот контур): `guardrails/gate-red-proofs.json`, `guardrails/hook-red-proofs.json`, `guardrails/gates-manifest.json`, `guardrails/ci-mirror.json`, `guardrails/judge-hooks.json`.

## Гейт a (prover record) и гейт s (skill review)

**Гейт a** — `guardrails/check-prover-record.sh` (443 строки). Вызывается из `guardrails/pre-push` (секция «gate a») и из `.github/workflows/gates.yml` (шаг «gate a»). Требует существования датированного сегодняшним числом файла `docs/prover/<today>-*.md` — записи «свежего перепрочтения» PRODUCT_SPEC.md и ARCHITECTURE.md плюс адверсариального прочтения именно пушимого диапазона коммитов (SPEC INV-304, «один рекорд на пуш» после слияния двух прежних требований). Поблажки (carve-outs), все с маркером `# STAND-DOWN: <name>`:
1. **deletion-only** — весь push состоит из удалений рефов; снимается ещё до цепочки букв, в `pre-push`.
2. **inbox-deposit** — диф состоит ровно из одного нового файла в `inbox/`.
3. **case-or-space** — весь диф — изменение регистра букв и/или пробелов (`guardrails/case_or_space_only.py`).
4. **recordless-class** — каждый коммит диапазона трогает только три «безрекордных» каталога: `docs/prover/`, `docs/skill-review/`, `docs/language-reads/` (сознательно сужено после adversarial-ревью 15.08.2026, находки F1–F3: более широкий класс когда-то позволил переписать сами правила и тест без записи).
5. **work-run road fallback** — если файла с сегодняшней датой нет, но существует более старая ещё «свежая» запись для обоих охраняемых документов — она принимается вместо новой.

Слабое место (декларируется самим кодом): запись — это markdown-файл, который агент пишет о своей же проверке; ничто механически не верифицирует, что заявленное ревью действительно состоялось или было строгим — гейт ловит только *отсутствие* записи, а не её фиктивность (докстринг сам признаёт: «дата только должна парситься»). Отсюда метка НЕЯСНО в таблице.

**Гейт s** — `guardrails/check-skill-review.sh` (174 строки). Вызывается из `guardrails/pre-push` («gate s») и `.github/workflows/gates.yml` («gate s»). Требует, чтобы «существенное» изменение файла под `skills/` (добавленная/удалённая содержательная строка, не version-stamp) в пушимом диапазоне сопровождалось коммитом в `docs/skill-review/`. Поблажки:
1. **case-or-space carve-out** — то же самое, что у гейта a (только регистр/пробелы).
2. **version-stamp-only bump** — чистый бамп номера версии в SKILL.md освобождён «by construction» (не считается существенным изменением).

Тот же структурный изъян, что у гейта a: запись ревью самозаявленная. Отличие в предмете — `skills/` это реально шипуемый пользователям артефакт (в отличие от PRODUCT_SPEC.md/ARCHITECTURE.md, которые описывают только внутренний процесс), поэтому по существу гейт s ближе к защите шипуемого продукта, но механизм проверки идентично слаб. Отсюда тоже НЕЯСНО, а не однозначная метка.
